build.what: Compiles the extension's TypeScript to out/ (tsc -p .). Fails on a type error.

review-stop.what: After build, run the CORE-GOV-15 regression for stopping a Review card's active acceptance worker and command. Requires an executed, passing named case.

review-regressions.run: node test/run.js --test-reporter=tap test/done-review.test.js test/finish.test.js test/checks.test.js test/review-webview.test.js test/review-eval.test.js eval/review/selftest.js
review-regressions.what: After the build check, tests Review evidence and verdicts, Finish, check receipts, review controls and the offline evaluation fixtures.

finish-regressions.run: node test/run.js --test-reporter=tap test/finish.test.js test/deliver.test.js test/checks.test.js test/full-test-lock.test.js
finish-regressions.what: After build, exercise Finish and delivery in throwaway Git repositories, check execution and the full-suite lock. Four of the test files, so it takes no suite lock and waits for no other run (test/full-test-lock.js: only a run of every test file takes it). Measured on Windows 11 (Ryzen 9 9950X, Node 26.7.0), 19 November 2026, before the merge with main: 385 s alone at 8d5e9887 (138 tests) and 424 s with the Finish acceptance tests added (146 tests). minutes is that run plus a quarter, rounded up. Linux: not measured.

finish-boundaries.run: node test/run.js --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern="F120:|deliver: two cards whose turns end together" test/orchestrator-board.test.js test/board.test.js
finish-boundaries.what: Exercise landed-only orchestrator Finish and simultaneous deliveries using local fixtures.

test.what: Compiles and runs all test/*.test.js, including mechanical parity. Windows needs the wrapper built first; browser and process checks require their local tools. Reports exact failures and skips.

parity.what: Compares media/board.js's visible text with docs/parity/FEATURES.md for this machine's side (tools/parity.js). Exit 1 on drift.

build-wrapper.what: Windows only: compiles wrapper/launcher.cs and wrapper/recorder.cs to wrapper/*.exe with the C# compiler that ships with .NET Framework 4.x (wrapper/build.ps1). On Linux there is no csc.exe, so this check fails there.

package.what: Builds and inspects the host package with pinned vsce 4.0.0. Checks selected runtime, legal and documentation entries against source. Installs and publishes nothing; inclusion checks do not establish content privacy. Initial npx use may need network access.

package-linux.what: Builds and inspects dist/entomatical-linux.vsix for linux-x64. May inspect its composition from Windows; this does not establish Linux runtime acceptance. Installs nothing.

helper-receipts.what: Read-only summary of the helper runs under .entomatical/helpers of this repository (F83). Exits 1 with 'No helper folder' when the worktree has none, which a fresh worktree does; use it only where helper runs exist.

replay-dry-run.what: Renders the authored public prompt-preparation regression cases without calling a model. No recorded helper inputs ship. Needs out/ built.

example-note.what: Used by docs/agents/examples/example.plan.json only: the note its steps write is added to git. Needs nothing installed, so it runs in a fresh step worktree.

battle-regressions.run: node test/run.js --test-reporter=tap test/battle.test.js test/extension-battle.test.js test/battle-orchestrator.test.js test/card-terminal.test.js test/card-terminal-control.test.js test/card-terminal-turn.test.js
battle-regressions.what: After build: Battle Royale's line-up and start, battle orchestrators, and card terminals' start-up answers and waiting prompts. Throwaway boards and stand-in terminals only.

vault-regressions.what: After build: Finish to a vault (F125) with throwaway repos, a local bare repository as the vault and a fake helper.

webview-regressions.run: node test/run.js --test-reporter=tap test/provider-ui-webview.test.js test/responsive-webview.test.js test/toggle-buttons-webview.test.js test/form-width-webview.test.js test/webview-gates.test.js
webview-regressions.what: After build: the board's form and cards in headless Chrome or Edge with the real media/board.js and board.css.

monitor-live-tests.what: Every test of the 3D Monitor working mock-up (ui-concepts/monitor-3d-live), run from the repository's top folder. Needs no build and no package. The page tests need Edge or Chrome and skip without one, so read the skip count. Measured on Windows 11, Node 26.7.0, 27 November 2026: 300 tests, 296 pass, 4 skipped, 61 s.
